sections.h2: How does Findlay's housing market work for a seller?
sections.html:
Findlay sells to people tied to the local payroll. The city is the seat of Hancock County and the second-largest in Northwest Ohio, roughly 40 miles south of Toledo, and its housing demand follows hiring at the refinery-era headquarters, appliance plant and hospital more than the season.

The Blanchard River cuts across town from east to west. The settlement began as Fort Findlay, a stockade raised in the War of 1812, and the first lots were platted in 1821. Oil and gas drilling in the 1880s lifted the population from 4,633 in 1880 to 18,553 by 1890, which is why blocks near downtown hold so much housing from that period. Subdivisions fill the rest of the 19.64 square miles of land.

An owner in town can hire an agent, go it alone, or deal with an investor directly, and the local details below change the math for each.

sections.h2: How pricey is a Findlay home by the Census numbers?
sections.html:
Findlay prices sit well under the Columbus and Cleveland suburbs. About 40 percent of households rent, so landlords and first-time buyers both shop here.

The 2020 count was 40,313, close to today's estimate, so rival listings rather than newcomers cap what a house fetches.

Other Census figures help frame a buyer: 91.0 percent of households have a broadband subscription, 30.6 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and the city counts 2,139 veterans. Remote workers weighing a Findlay purchase will read the broadband line first.

sections.h2: How does the Blanchard River affect selling a Findlay house?
sections.html:
Flood exposure is the first property-specific question Findlay buyers and lenders raise. The river crested at 18.46 feet in 2007, causing around $100 million in damage and coming close to the 1913 record.

The city floodplain page lays out what an owner should know:

  • The city participates in the National Flood Insurance Program, so any parcel can be insured through it or a private carrier.
  • Grading, new construction and alterations inside a Special Flood Hazard Area need a Flood Development Permit before work begins.
  • Structural damage in that area, from flood, fire, wind or anything else, goes to the Zoning Department for a damage assessment.
  • The Hancock County Auditor maps show whether a given parcel sits in the hazard area, and zoning staff will help read them.

After the first phase of river benching, the city sent FEMA a Letter of Map Revision proposing to remove or shrink flood zones over a significant amount of land, and the flood information page links a parcel list. See whether your lot is named before choosing a list price, since a revised map can lower or raise a buyer's insurance premium.

Weather also tests the structure. NOAA normals on the city's Wikipedia page show about 37.7 inches of precipitation and 23.8 inches of snow a year, so buyers poke at roof edges, downspouts and damp basement corners.

sections.h2: Which Findlay employers and roads feed buyer demand?
sections.html:
Few cities Findlay's size depend on such a short list of big names. Marathon Petroleum has its headquarters downtown, Whirlpool operates what is considered the world's largest dishwasher plant by output, and Lowe's, Kohl's, Best Buy and Campbell Soup run distribution centers here. Cooper Tire, founded in Findlay in 1914, came under Goodyear in 2021.

The largest local payrolls, per the 2024 city financial report quoted on Wikipedia:

  • Blanchard Valley Regional Health Center, 3,165 employees
  • Marathon Petroleum, 2,159
  • Whirlpool, 1,930
  • Goodyear, 895
  • Findlay City Schools, 865
  • The University of Findlay, 548

Interstate 75 crosses the city, US 68 ends here, and US 224 plus Ohio routes 12, 15, 37 and 568 all pass through. The University of Findlay enrolls over 4,100 students and Owens Community College adds more, so a rental or starter home near campus has its own buyer group. Public school students attend Findlay City Schools, and Findlay High School covers grades 9 to 12.

sections.h2: What does Hancock County charge to transfer a Findlay deed?
sections.html:
The county Auditor takes $3 for every thousand dollars conveyed, rounded to the nearest ten cents, and adds $0.50 per parcel. Some transfers are exempt from the conveyance portion.

According to the Hancock County property transfer page, the Auditor needs a DTE 100 statement of value (or a DTE 100(EX) when an exemption applies) and a notarized deed whose legal description is exact. Checks are written to the Hancock County Auditor. Staff in the Real Estate Division, room 21 of the courthouse, take questions at 419-424-7015.

Filing with the recorder comes next. The recorder's fee schedule charges $39 for the first two pages of a document and $8 for each additional page, a rate that began in January 2025. Ohio requires the signature on the deed to be acknowledged before a notary or similar officer (ORC 5301.01).

sections.h2: What else shapes a Findlay neighborhood besides the river?
sections.html:
Findlay brands itself Flag City, USA, and the calendar gives buyers a feel for daily life: Boogie on the Block in June, the Flag City BalloonFest in August, then Oktoberfest and a Halloween parade in the fall, with the Hancock County Fair as an anchor.

The Findlay Reservoir No. 2, at roughly 5 billion gallons, is the largest above-ground reservoir in Ohio. Riverside Park holds the weir on the Blanchard, the Findlay-Hancock County Public Library has served the city since 1888, and the University of Findlay runs a 152-acre farm for its equestrian and pre-veterinary students. Findlay Airport lies about two nautical miles south-southwest of the central business district. Findlay was also the first community in the world to offer touch-tone telephone service, which began on November 1, 1960.

Mention them in a listing: a short drive to the park, school or plant gate is often the first question.

sections.h2: What must a Findlay seller hand the buyer?
sections.html:
Ohio's residential disclosure statute (ORC 5302.30) has the seller fill in a condition form for the buyer. Late delivery opens a three business day window for the buyer to walk away.

The statute exempts estate fiduciaries, heirs who never lived in the home and family transfers, a list that fits Findlay's many long-held family houses.

sections.h2: What are the practical ways to sell a Findlay house?
sections.html:
Your repair list and your deadline decide which route fits.

  • Agent listing: the most exposure, with closing set by showings and the buyer's lender.
  • Sale by owner: no commission, but forms and deed prep are yours.
  • Cash purchase: no lender or appraisal, and you pick the closing day, at a price that reflects the repairs.
  • Family or neighbor sale: friendlier talks and the same Auditor paperwork.

Line up two written offers and compare what each leaves you after fees, tax proration and payoff.

faqs.q: Does a Findlay home near the river sell for less?
faqs.a: It can, since flood insurance adds a cost for the buyer. Pull the parcel on the Hancock County Auditor maps, ask Zoning about the pending map revision, and keep any elevation certificate or insurance records handy.

faqs.q: What is the Hancock County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The Auditor charges $3 per $1,000 conveyed and $0.50 per parcel, with recording billed separately by the recorder. Call the Real Estate Division for the total on your deed.

faqs.q: Do I have to repair a Findlay house before selling?
faqs.a: Ohio sets no repair requirement for a sale. Known problems go on the disclosure form, and a lender-backed buyer may negotiate fixes after the inspection.

faqs.q: Where is the deed filed once a Findlay sale closes?
faqs.a: With the Hancock County Recorder, once the Auditor has endorsed it. Until recorded, a deed is fraudulent against a later good-faith buyer (ORC 5301.25), so closers file fast.

faqs.q: Who buys houses in Findlay besides families?
faqs.a: Landlords and investors do, since roughly 40 percent of households rent at a median of $975. Plant, hospital and university employees add to the buyer pool.
